question: Can direct numerical construction acquire an entire hidden state-transition map, rather than just one residual output bit on a supplied rotation?
hypothesis: Basis interrogation builds unknown affine coefficients, then counterexample-minimized feature growth can acquire some complete vector nonlinear transition maps. Probe budget, output-cancellation and incorrect minimal features should expose failures; fully known affine success alone is insufficient for nonlinear support.
world: Each action is an unknown vector-valued GF2 polynomial. Each output has hidden random bias and four distinct linear inputs. Nonlinear families add four/eight distinct monomials of random degree2..4, each with independent random nonzero output-vector coefficient. All matrix, bias, support and output coefficients hidden. Learner receives only width, budget and genuine full-state transition replies. No fixed rotation or known output map.
learner: Query zero and every singleton (width+1 observations/action) to directly construct bias and linear vector coefficients. Then cycle real all-ones/random states (.5/.75/.875, fixed policy seed1997+width). Replay cached contradictions first. Select lowest differing output bit and greedily remove set input bits while that output's residual stays1. XOR full residual vector at remaining witness into a newly allocated mask feature (or existing coefficient). Any degree0..width allowed; cap width+1+32 cells/action and256 updates/action. Cached actual responses stored/counted. No hidden source or mask enumeration. Budget exhaustion during minimization preserves current model.
trained_control: Closed-form conventional shared Hamming RBF Gram/Cholesky interpolation k=2^(-Hamming), one output coefficient vector per source input. Fit every observed output bit to max residual<=1e-7. Rounding12 decimals at threshold.5. This is trained kernel regression, not matched strongest neural control; all coefficients, input centers, probe cache and all-in time counted.

tests.heldout_sampling: with replacement excluding active training action/state pairs
tests.exact_structure: evaluator compares all learned vector coefficients with hidden full polynomial; never supplies parameters to learner
tests.retention: second independent full map acquired, no collateral first-world weight mutation; separate queries/cost reported
tests.controls: no fixed background; basis-only must fail on hidden nonlinear features where exposed; retain all errors and cached contradictions

thresholds.engineering: all mandatory previous regression and WSP42 tests plus clean tree/source atlas Windows/Linux; identical integer primary scores/trace
thresholds.affine: all affine128 source coefficients exactly recovered and all unseen states/compositions/goals correct
thresholds.nonlinear: on four_nonlinear128, >=95% exact one-step,>=90% composition/plans,>=90% exact action maps and >=10pp one-step gain over basis-only. All widths and seeds included, no filtering. Eight-term boundary reported separately.
thresholds.scientific: DEV_SUPPORTED only if affine and nonlinear bounds both pass, MIXED if affine bound only or partial nonlinear recovery; SCIENTIFIC_NEGATIVE if neither; INVALID on oracle leaks/protocol drift. No independent SCIENTIFIC_PASS or general intelligence without novel domains and matched strongest neural baselines.

authority: Isolated contributor draft public synthetic research only; no merge/main, official loops, self-hosted runners, protected first-use, accepted refs, controller, scheduler, paid API, deployment or live actions.
limits: Input bits and action identity explicitly given; state representation and search machinery supplied.
AND/XOR and affine priors are preauthored. All learned transition coefficients start unknown, but the discovery algorithm remains external Python software.
Converged kernel fit does not imply strongest neural comparator or matched capacity/cost.
No ground-up general intelligence claim from a synthetic full-map experiment.
